title.narrative: Institutionalise and strengthen capacity development to sustain identification and the safeguarding of World Cultural and Natural Heritage in Africa

description.narrative: To guide the implementation of this Flagship Programme, the World Heritage Centre developed the Strategy for World Heritage in Africa (2022-2029), which the World Heritage Committee adopted at its extended 45th session in Riyadh (2023). In line with this, this project aims to foster the capacities of higher learning institutions and universities to enhance the implementation of the World Heritage Convention. It will facilitate the establishment and operationalisation of a Pan-African Network of Universities and Higher Learning Institutions, including the creation of five education centres, one in each subregion (Southern, East, Central, West, and North Africa), to enhance and/or develop heritage curriculums, support heritage-related processes (nomination, conservation and management) and promote inter-regional experience-sharing. This includes also providing training and exchanges of knowledge among African and Korean heritage experts and World Heritage sites, therefore strengthening the capacities of professionals from both sides in tackling global challenges such as climate change, striking a balance between conservation and development, promoting sustainable tourism, interpretation, etc.
